title: Ear tube inflation
what: The doctor blows air into the ear tubes, the channels that connect the nose and the ear. This helps even out the pressure in the ear.
why: For a blocked ear after a cold or a flight, an ear infection with fluid, or reduced hearing.
duration: usually 5 to 15 minutes; a course is several sessions
tell_doctor: If your nose is blocked or runny
If you had ear or nose surgery
If you recently had a bad ear infection

prepare.title: Nose
prepare.text: If your nose is blocked, the doctor may put in decongestant drops.

steps: The doctor checks your ears and nose
Sometimes drops are put in your nose
A tip is placed in one nostril, and the other is pressed closed
You are asked to say a word or swallow
At that moment, a puff of air is given
feel: You feel a push of air in the ear
You may hear a noise or a pop in the ear
A slightly unpleasant feeling in the nose
after: The blocked feeling usually eases right away or after a few sessions
Do not blow your nose hard
The course and drops are as your doctor prescribes
red_flags: Severe ear pain after the procedure
Discharge or blood from the ear

faq.a: When it is done for the right reasons, it is a safe procedure.

faq.q: Can I inflate my ears myself?
faq.a: Not without your doctor's advice. You can do harm.

reminders.text: Ear tube inflation tomorrow. If your nose is blocked, tell the doctor.
